sanskrit_verse:
श्रीकामः शान्तिकामो वा ग्रहयज्ञं समाचरेत् ।
वृष्ट्यायुःपुष्टिकामो वा तथैवाभिचरन्नपि ॥१.२९५
transliteration: śrīkāmaḥ śāntikāmo vā grahayajñaṃ samācaret | vṛṣṭyāyuḥpuṣṭikāmo vā tathaivābhicarann api ||1.295||
sph_interpretive_translation: One desiring prosperity, peace, rainfall, longevity, or nourishment shall perform the Graha Yajna; even one who has erred in conduct must execute it for restoration.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from intent aligned with cosmic order
Causation arises through ritual action, not moral judgment
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious participation in dharma
Restoration logic operates through completion of prescribed action
Consciousness alignment occurs via precise execution of Vedic injunction
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent desires material or spiritual benefit THEN agent SHALL perform Graha Yajna
IF agent has acted contrary to dharma THEN agent SHALL perform Graha Yajna FOR restoration
NO punitive consequence SHALL be enforced INSTEAD OF ritual completion
RITUAL performance SHALL overwrite karmic misalignment WITHOUT retribution
AGENT’S capacity SHALL be restored UPON correct ritual enactment
supreme_court_application: In Supreme adjudication, desire for societal benefit or personal correction invokes mandatory performance of Graha Yajna. Legal standing derives not from fault but from alignment-seeking. The court directs ritual completion as constitutional obligation overriding punitive measures.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that causal efficacy lies in yajña, not in punitive attribution. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential purification through ritual. Responsibility aligns proportionally with conscious invocation of dharma, not past error. Non-punitive reality is upheld as ritual rectifies without condemnation.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate supervised Graha Yajna protocol upon declaration of intent
Assign dharmic facilitator to ensure procedural accuracy
Validate completion through Vedic witness mechanism
Reintegrate individual into societal dharma cycle post-performance
Restore capacity through affirmation of completed duty
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands declared: Śrīkāmaḥ śāntikāmo vā performs Graha Yajna. Dharma is restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
